Next, use the Trace tool to select only half of the pattern, press Enter, and create an internal line identical to that segment. Double-click the internal line with the Edit Pattern tool to select it, copy it, and paste it onto the crown front, where the graphic will be placed. Then, using the Transform Pattern tool, adjust the internal line on the crown pattern so it aligns with the outline. If any part of the internal line doesn't align perfectly, right-click the points on that internal line with the Edit Pattern tool, select to pattern outline under the Extend Trim Add Point options, and let it snap to the outline, creating a segment point at the contact. Now, select all the internal lines on the pattern with the applied graphic using the Edit Pattern tool and delete them. Then, use the Segment Sewing tool to sew the pattern. For a more natural graphic appearance, select the sewing line with the Edit Sewing tool, remove the normal map applied to the 3D seam line map, and set both intensity and thickness to 0. Finally, choose the Superimpose to place it on the outside of the crown and run the simulation. Now, let's apply fabrics to the finished hat pattern. Press Y on your keyboard to open the library. Click the Fabric tab where you can select preset fabrics provided by Clow. In the search bar, type Twill. Double-click the heavy twill fabric, the first one in the list, to add it to the Fabric tab in the Object Browser. Next, search for Lining. Double-click the polyester satin lining fabric, the second one in the list, to add it to the Fabric tab. Lastly, search for Trim. You'll see a hardware material for trims at the top of the list. Double-click it as well to add it to the Fabric tab in the Object Browser. Since we're using arbitrary fabrics, apply the heavy twill fabric to all patterns except the bias tape, snap, and eyelets. Then, apply the lining fabric to the bias tape and the trim hardware fabric to the snap. Now we've finished everything, from the basic construction of the hat to all the detailed trims. For the final step, let's use the Solidify function to keep the hat's current shape while still allowing for natural simulation. Select the visor pattern and in the Property Editor, turn Solidify On. As I mentioned earlier, this option controls how much of the current simulated shape is maintained. Set the Solidify strength of the visor to 80, then select all patterns and set them to Unstrengthen. Run the simulation, and you'll see the visor hold its general shape while still bending into a natural angle. And that completes the process of creating a cap using the mold profile and visor provided as Connect assets. Use this tutorial as a reference and try designing your own hat with the cap asset.

The newly released cap molds and visors are available in both men's and women's versions and support a variety of design styles. For the cap molds, three different profiles are provided for men and women respectively. For the visors, a total of four types are available, allowing for various brim curvatures. We'll be using the commonly used middle profile mold and a half-curved visor. Once you've downloaded them, let's import the middle profile mold into Claw. When you import the mold, you'll notice the ear dummy. We'll be designing the hat to sit above the ears so that it doesn't pass through. If you're working on a design that covers the ears, right-click above the ear dummy and select **Deactivate Avatar** to disable it. Then, in the Property Editor, set the opacity to 0 to proceed with the creation. ## Step 2: Guidelines for Design The mold files provided by Connect come with pre-drawn guidelines to make designing easier. You can either use these lines as they are or draw your own if needed. In this video, we'll start by showing you how to draw simple guidelines. First, activate the **Show 3D Pen** and **Show Avatar Measure** icons from the Avatar Display menu at the top left. This will display all the guidelines needed for hat making. Among these, we'll delete the **Circumference** guideline and redraw it. 1. From the 3D toolbar, select the **Edit Measure** tool, click on the purple line, and press **Delete**. 2. Next, select the **Edit 3D Pen** tool, double-click on the black line to select all of it, and press **Delete**. 3. Select the **3D Avatar Pen** tool located under the Edit 3D Pen tool, and click a point above the ear dummy. 4. Then choose **Maintain Curve** to turn them into curve points. Once the pattern modifications are complete, click the **Transform Pattern** tool in the 2D toolbar and select all patterns in the 2D window. Finally, for a stable simulation, right-click on the patterns and choose **Strengthen** before running the simulation. While drawing the back opening line, hold down the **ctrl** key to create it as a curve. After drawing the line, use the **Edit Curve Point** tool to refine it into the desired shape.
